bib.title: Pretraining Data Mixtures Enable Narrow Model Selection Capabilities in Transformer Models

question: How well can transformers pretrained on a mixture of distinct function families identify a task family in-context and learn within it, and do they generalize to functions outside that mixture?
hypothesis: In-context learning ability is tied to coverage of the pretraining data mixture rather than to an inductive bias for general extrapolation.
contributions: Pretrain transformers for ICL on mixtures of multiple function classes and characterize the model selection behavior
Study ICL behavior on functions out-of-distribution from the pretraining function classes
Strong evidence of model selection among pretrained classes at little extra statistical cost, limited evidence of generalizing beyond pretraining data

method.summary: Decoder-only transformers are trained from scratch on simulated prompts of (x,f(x)) pairs, f drawn from a weighted mixture of function classes (dense linear, sparse linear, two-layer ReLU, sinusoid). They are then evaluated in-context on in-mixture and out-of-distribution functions (convex combinations, extreme-frequency sinusoids).
method.task: in-context learning of function classes (regression), model selection and OOD generalization

datasets.name: Simulated function-class prompts
datasets.size: inferred: 1M steps x batch 1024 prompts; text says approx. 1 billion examples used in pretraining (sinusoid experiment)
datasets.source: Generated: x~N(0,I_d), d=20 (d=1 for sinusoids); dense beta~N(0,I_d), f=beta^T x/sqrt(d); sparse s non-zero coords N(0,1), f=beta^T x/sqrt(s); ReLU 2-layer d_h=100, W_ij~N(0,2), f=beta^T relu(Wx)/(sqrt(d) d_h); sine f=beta cos(2 pi omega x), omega~Gamma(6,1/6), beta~N(0,1)
datasets.preprocessing: Variances of f(x) equalised across classes; f(x) zero-padded to d dims; no label noise in reported results

models.name: GPT-2-scale decoder (Garg et al. config)
models.architecture: decoder-only transformer, cosine positional embeddings, learnable linear in/out projections

training.objective: teacher-forcing squared loss on f(x) positions (Eq. 2.1)

other.learning rate note: 'learning rate of 1' as printed, empirically tuned (Pax/Adam scaling likely)
other.tokenized attempt: 5M epochs cross-entropy on binned scalars, loss not significantly decreased

inference.prompting: prompt = (x1,f(x1),...,xn,f(xn),x_{n+1}); n up to 40 in-context points in curves; 16 in Fig 1 and 3

metrics.name: Normalized mean squared difference
metrics.definition: MSD between mixture-model and sparse- or dense-only predictions, normalized by MSD between sparse and dense models

baselines: Models pretrained on a single function class (w=0 or 1)
eval.protocol: Mostly figures; no seeds, error bars or significance tests stated

results.claim: A model pretrained on a dense+sparse linear mixture matches single-class models on in-mixture functions, i.e. near-zero cost of in-context model selection.
results.setup: Synthetic (x, f(x)) in-context regression, d=20, 9.5M-param GPT-2-scale decoder trained from scratch on simulated function classes; not natural language; Fig 1-3, w in {0,.25,.5,.75,1}
results.quote: We have empirically shown that for task families or function classes well-represented in the pretraining mixture, cost of selecting the appropriate function class to use for in-context learning is nearly zero.

results.claim: A model trained only on sparse linear functions does poorly on dense linear prompts and vice versa, though both are linear.
results.setup: Synthetic (x, f(x)) in-context regression, d=20, 9.5M-param GPT-2-scale decoder trained from scratch on simulated function classes; not natural language
results.quote: Even though dense and sparse linear classes are both linear functions, we can see the poor performance of the red curve in Figure 2a

results.claim: Mixture-trained model fails on a convex combination (weighted sum of y-values) of linear and cosine functions.
results.setup: Synthetic (x, f(x)) in-context regression, d=20, 9.5M-param GPT-2-scale decoder trained from scratch on simulated function classes; not natural language, 1-D, 0.5 linear + 0.5 sine mixture
results.quote: it is unable to fit a function that is a convex combination of the two

results.claim: Sinusoid frequency below 0.01 or above 5 is extremely rare in pretraining, and predictions degrade there.
results.setup: Synthetic (x, f(x)) in-context regression, d=20, 9.5M-param GPT-2-scale decoder trained from scratch on simulated function classes; not natural language; sinusoid frequencies Gamma(6,1/6), mean 1
results.quote: the probability of a sampling a frequency outside this range is less than 1 × 10−7

results.claim: In-context model-selection ability improves with model size, asymmetrically across function classes.
results.quote: we observe the general trend that the ability to perform model selection increases as models get larger

results.setup: Synthetic (x, f(x)) in-context regression, d=20, 9.5M-param GPT-2-scale decoder trained from scratch on simulated function classes; not natural language
results.quote: We use a 9.5M parameter decoder model with 12 layers, 8 attention heads,

results.claim: Mixture model's predictions at moderate sparsity (nnz about 4) lie between the sparse-only and dense-only models, not equal to either.
results.setup: Synthetic (x, f(x)) in-context regression, d=20, 9.5M-param GPT-2-scale decoder trained from scratch on simulated function classes; not natural language, 16 in-context examples
results.quote: the mixture predictions deviate from both those of the purely dense or purely sparse pretrained transformer

results.claim: Authors conclude ICL ability may track pretraining mixture coverage more than inductive bias for generalization.
results.quote: the impressive ICL abilities of high-capacity sequence models may be more closely tied to the coverage of their pretraining data mixtures

limits: Only synthetic function classes with real-valued inputs; no natural-language model tested.
Authors' tokenized (binned) language-model attempt did not train: loss not significantly decreased after 5M epochs.
Single small model (9.5M; 0.2M, 1.2M for size), no seeds or error bars reported.
Fig 1 bar values are only legible as unordered numbers in the text layer, so not recorded as results.
Notions of task family, mixture and convex combination are unclear for natural language (authors).
